text:
maria: quick heads-up — onboarding HF->Redwood conversion for model 'astra-7b' shows a small but repeatable quality regression when prompts contain non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) or some leading combining marks. looks like pretokenizer normalization + byte-fallback order changed during conversion. anyone seen this?
kevin: saw the alert on perf dashboard earlier, nice catch. do you have a tiny repro?
maria: minimal repro attached inline. hf tokenizer (python) vs converted rw tokenizer:
```python
# HF
>>> tokenizer.encode('Hello\u00A0world').tokens
['Hello', '\u00A0world']
# Redwood runtime after conversion
>>> tokenizer.encode('Hello\u00A0world').tokens
['Hello', 'world']
```
so HF keeps the NBSP as a separate token piece while RW conversion normalized it away (merged into space) which shifted prefix cache/keying for chat templates and changed completion sampling.
asim: interesting — two likely culprits: 1) normalizer in tokenizer config.json mapped to NFKC vs NFC (HF default sometimes uses NFC), 2) byte-fallback / pre-tokenizer ordering changed so NBSP becomes part of whitespace run. also watch out for special tokens used by our chat templates (e.g., "<|system|>" and leading space tokens).
leo: had a similar hit with leading nonbreaking-space in a customer prompt last quarter. we ended up adding a conservative preprocessor to preserve NBSP -> map to MARKER token before tokenization then restore. messy but effective.
eval-bot: regression: +3.1% failure rate on prompt-normalization suite after quantization+conversion (detected 2026-03-19 21:04Z) :warning:
buildbot: conversion job #4822 posted logs: https://ci.redwood/conv/4822 — shows config.json normalized: "normalize": true and "normalizer": "nqkc" (typo?)
kevin: typo in config.json normalizer field? that could explain divergent behavior. can you paste the converted config snippet?
maria: here's the relevant fragment from converted tokenizer.json: 
```json
{"normalizer": {"type": "replace", "pattern": "\u00A0", "with": " "}, "pre_tokenizer": {"type": "whitespace_split"}, "byte_fallback": true}
```
that replace is too aggressive for our chat workloads. HF's tokenizer sometimes keeps NBSP as separate token, depending on pre-tokenization rules.
asim: plan: 1) update HF->RW conversion to preserve explicit normalizer types (NFC/NFKC/NFD) and the order of byte fallback vs whitespace pretokenizer; 2) add unit tests with NBSP, ZERO-WIDTH-SPACE, combining marks, and leading spaces in chat templates; 3) short-term workaround: patch the conversion to map NBSP -> U+E000 marker token (private use) instead of plain space.
kevin: +1. also add a canary on dedicated for a day before rolling to hosted. keep batching/caching config identical so we isolate tokenization.
maria: adding conversion patch now. quick patch diff: 
```diff
- normalizer: {"type": "replace", "pattern": "\u00A0", "with": " "}
+ normalizer: {"type": "identity_if_preserve_nbsp"} # preserve NBSP until tokenization step
+ preprocessor: {"map_nbsp_to_marker": "\uE000"}
```
will push as a canary branch and run the prompt-normalization suite.
leo: tiny note — watch chat template leading-space semantics. some HF chat models expect a leading space token before user messages; if conversion strips it, that shifts all token IDs and causes off-by-one for cache keys. test that with our chat_template fixture.
maria: good catch — will add explicit tests for chat templates and function-calling prompts.
eval-bot: queued rerun of the prompt-normalization suite (includes INF/chat_template tests) — ETA ~35m.
buildbot: canary build 2026-03-19T22:10Z started on dedicated cluster rw-ded-3.
kevin: thanks — ping here if metrics look better.
maria: patch pushed to branch `conv/preserve-nbsp`, adding tests + doc note about normalizer differences. rolling to canary now.
asim: awesome, thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
leo: if the canary is green, follow-up action: publish an RFC to set default conversion to preserve non-spacing characters unless explicitly configured.
maria: agree. will open RFC after canary.
kevin: great thread, please add the reproducer to the model onboarding checklist so SRE/ML don't miss it next time.
